title: Sen. Shelley Capito Disclosed 4 Stock Sales: Apple, Microsoft, Meta and Zoetis
content:
Sen. Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV) disclosed four stock sales on November 4, 2026, all dated October 21: Apple, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Zoetis, each in the $1,001–$15,000 band.

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

DateTickerCompanyType / sizePrice at trade vs. Nov 9 (Bargo est.)
Oct 21AAPLApple Inc.Sale, $1,001–$15,000$343.99 vs. $350.69 (+1.95%)
Oct 21METAMeta Platforms, Inc.Sale, $1,001–$15,000$697.52 vs. $641.37 (−8.05%)
Oct 21MSFTMicrosoft CorporationSale, $1,001–$15,000$532.95 vs. $545.18 (+2.29%)
Oct 21ZTSZoetis Inc.Sale, $1,001–$15,000$79.62 vs. $82.32 (+3.39%)

Transaction date for all four: Oct 21, 2026. Disclosure date: Nov 4, 2026 (14 days later). Member: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, WV (Senate).

What's been disclosed

  • Four sales: Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Meta Platforms (META) and Zoetis (ZTS), $1,001–$15,000 each, all on October 21.
  • Price since: Bargo's estimate puts Meta about 8.1% lower on November 9 than on October 21, Zoetis about 3.4% higher, Microsoft about 2.3% higher and Apple about 2.0% higher.
  • Timing: the filing came 14 days after the trades, well inside the 45-day window.

Quick FAQ

How long after the trades were they disclosed?
14 days after the trades, which were all dated October 21. The STOCK Act gives members 45 days from the transaction to disclose it.

Why are the amounts ranges?
Filings report value bands such as $15,001–$50,000 instead of exact dollar amounts.

Where does the price comparison come from?
It is Bargo's estimate, comparing the price on the transaction date with the November 9 price. It is not the member's actual execution price.
